parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
From Source 1, identify the trend in the number of people in the world without access to
electricity.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: From Source 2, identify two consequences of energy poverty.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Which consequence of energy poverty do you think is the most significant? Explain why.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why energy poverty is an important personal issue.

text: Study Sources 1 to 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘The world’s energy problems must be solved by the rich industrialised countries.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Rich industrialised nations emit the most greenhouse gases.’
How could you test this claim? You should consider the types of information, sources of
evidence and methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one opinion from Hua’s statement. Explain why it is an opinion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Jin argues that energy poverty is best solved at the local level.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify one fact from Jin’s statement.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain how well this fact supports Jin’s argument.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Hua’s or Jin’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments, and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
Your government wants to reduce energy poverty.
The following actions are being considered:
• Increasing access to electricity through national projects.
• Investing in microgrids producing renewable energy.
• Teaching local people about energy efficiency.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
